Awesome AI for Astronomy

 A curated list of papers, models, datasets, benchmarks and software for artificial intelligence in astronomy, astrophysics, cosmology, heliophysics and planetary science. 

 
 
 
 
 

 Web page     AstroAI Today     Contents     Contributing     Citation 

 

 [!TIP]
 The searchable web page filters all 482 papers and 66 software packages by section, year, venue type, public code, model weights or data, and data modality, and shows a one-sentence summary for every paper. The full list can also be downloaded as JSON or CSV.
 
 AstroAI Today collects new arXiv papers on machine learning in astronomy every day. A language model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) screens them and writes a one-line TL;DR for each paper and a TL;DR for each week and month. These papers are not reviewed; the curated list below is.
 
 Use the AstroAI Research skill in compatible AI tools to query the curated catalogue and AstroAI Today.

 About

This list tracks machine learning work in astronomy with public papers, linking public code where it exists. It emphasises foundation models, language models, agents and benchmarks released since 2021, together with established deep learning methods in each subfield. General astronomy resources are covered by awesome-astronomy, and classical astronomical data science by awesome-astro-datascience.

 [!NOTE]
 - Papers are listed newest first within each subsection. The date column gives the month of the first arXiv version, or the publication year when there is no arXiv version.
 - Peer-reviewed venues are shown in bold when confirmed by the journal DOI, the official repository or the publisher page. Other entries show arXiv and the year. Oral, spotlight and award papers carry a separate tag.
 - Every arXiv identifier, DOI and repository link was checked against the paper page or the official repository before inclusion. Hovering over a paper title shows its summary.
